Class ServerRMIConnection

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am43.network.rmi.ServerRMIConnection
All Implemented Interfaces:
PersistentServerConnection, ServerConnection, VirtualClientRmi, VirtualClient, Remote
public class ServerRMIConnection extends Object implements PersistentServerConnection, VirtualClientRmi
Client-side "brain" representing the connection to the server over RMI. It exports itself as the client stub and holds remote, the server connection's stub, on which it invokes commands and pings directly across the network. It owns the HeartBeat and manages the lifecycle (lookup + handshake in open(), with retries, and teardown in disconnect()). It is the RMI counterpart of SocketServerConnection.

      public ServerRMIConnection(String serverIp, int port, String accessPointName, ServerConnectionUser connectionUser, MessageReceiver messageReceiver, UUID id)
      Parameters:
      serverIp - the server host to connect to
      port - the RMI registry port
      accessPointName - the name the access point is bound to in the registry
      connectionUser - callback notified when the server connection is lost
      messageReceiver - where incoming messages are forwarded (the client controller)
      id - this client's persistent unique identifier

  • Method Details

    • open

      public void open()
      Connects to the server: looks up the access point in the registry, exports this object as the client stub, calls connect() to perform the handshake and obtain the server stub, then starts the heartbeat. On failure it keeps retrying every few seconds until it succeeds.
      Specified by:

    • ping

      public void ping()
      Pings the server through the stub. The call is synchronous: its successful return is itself the keep-alive acknowledgement, so the pong timestamp is refreshed right after.
      Specified by:
      ping in interface PersistentServerConnection
